question: If a surgeon discovers an incidental finding during an operation, it is ethically and legally acceptable to excise it in the same sitting without prior consent, provided it is clinically indicated.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is false. Operating on an incidental finding not covered by the original consent violates consent principles — consent is procedure-specific. The exception is an immediate threat to life. All elective findings must be discussed postoperatively and consented before any further procedure.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct — this statement is FALSE. Consent is procedure-specific. Excising a structure not covered by the original consent constitutes an assault unless the patient would otherwise face immediate life-threatening harm. This must be deferred and consented separately.
